papers.title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
papers.abstract: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.
authors: K. Mahesh Krishna

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.
authors: Yisong Yang

papers.title: An exactly solvable obstructed seam on a lattice Klein bottle: bulk-locked Majorana rings and register-dependent toric codes
papers.abstract: We study a frustrated seam produced by literal reflection gluing of Wen's plaquette model on a closed lattice Klein bottle. The seam operators anticommute along two cycles for even circumference and one cycle of twice the length for odd circumference. Their algebra reduces to free Majorana rings, while the commuting bulk stabilizers constrain the allowed ring sectors. This bulk locking yields exact ground energies, excitation gaps and degeneracies, checked by phase-aware Pauli traces and finite-size diagonalization, including two 24-qubit energy predictions. The seam degeneracy is not topological: the single-site seam fields tested split it at second order. We contrast this obstructed gluing with consistent toric-code realizations. An edge register preserves the anyon labels; a Hadamard-dressed site register has colour-dependent seam transport, with ground-state degeneracy 2 or 4 for even circumference and a sign-frustrated exception at odd circumference. For the enumerated lattice isometries and sizes, we compute logical gates and distances, distinguishing abstract qubit relabelling from local hardware depth. Finally, on three 16- and 24-qubit lattices, chiral matter selects a holonomy doublet whose electric-field splitting follows two competing tunnelling routes. These matter results remain finite-size statements. The main result is the exact obstructed-seam solution with bulk sector locking; the register, gate and matter calculations delimit its relation to topological codes.
authors: Junhao (Eigen), Wang

papers.title: Stability analysis of the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$ describing polytropic gas spheres
papers.abstract:
We study the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$, the critical polytropic case separating finite-radius from infinite-radius self-gravitating equilibria. The scaling family $	heta_\lambda(\xi)=\lambda^{1/2}	heta(\lambda\xi)$ generates a neutral mode $\phi_0=	frac12	heta+\xi	heta'$ about the Schuster profile. Schuster's transformation and a logarithmic variable reduce the equation to the autonomous Hamiltonian system $\ddot
u=	frac14(
u-
u^5)$ with a first integral. Besides the Schuster (separatrix) and Srivastava solutions, every orbit crossing $
u=0$ is given in closed form by a Weierstrass $\wp$-function, and the closed forms agree with direct numerical integration to about $10^{-12}$. Up to scaling and sign, the Schuster solution is the only solution regular at the center, and it separates positive solutions from solutions with infinitely many zeros. In homology-invariant variables the singular solution $	heta=(2\xi)^{-1/2}$ is a center exactly at $n=5$, where its stability changes. For a distance-varying Emden--Fowler system with a shifted equilibrium we prove that at $n=5$ the unique equilibrium is linearly and nonlinearly unstable. Finally, the linearization about the Schuster profile is the Schr"odinger operator $L=-\Delta_r-5	heta_S^4$ on $L^2((0,\infty),\xi^2d\xi)$. Its Friedrichs extension has essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$, a threshold resonance at $0$ carried by the non-normalizable scaling mode, and exactly one negative eigenvalue, $\lambda_0\approx-1.21$, so the Schuster profile is a saddle point of the associated energy functional.
authors: S. C. Mancas, Ronald Adams

papers.title: Closure of Traceful Radiation-Gauge Reconstruction with Matter: General Kerr Conditions, a Thin-Shell Benchmark, and a Conserved Torus
papers.abstract: We formulate the closure problem for first-order, traceful radiation-gauge metric reconstruction on a Kerr background with matter. The reconstruction is decomposed into Weyl-curvature, Ricci-trace, and mass--angular-momentum completion sectors. For compatible initial, gauge, and completion data, we establish local existence and uniqueness of the resulting triangular transport system on a regular Kerr domain, and identify the additional conditions needed for a closed global formulation. This is not a global existence theorem. We test the framework using two conserved matter sources. For a thin shell around a Schwarzschild black hole, Israel matching, regularity, asymptotic flatness, a barotropic equation of state, and fixed rest mass determine the static, axial, and leading rotational sectors. The ADM-mass shift is $\sqrt{1-2M/R}$ times the shell rest mass, while the axial sector determines the angular momentum, moment of inertia, and interior frame dragging. We also construct a stationary constant-angular-momentum fluid torus on Kerr and compute its Newman--Penrose Ricci projections, showing that nonspherical sources generally excite coupled Ricci sectors. The shell provides a closed benchmark, while the torus illustrates the additional structure required for general Kerr sources.
authors: G. G. L. Nashed

papers.title: Clock--WEP Tests of String-Derived Dilaton and Modulus Sectors
papers.abstract: String compactifications and runaway-dilaton models can contain light scalar directions. Motion along these directions changes gauge couplings, the QCD scale, quark masses, and Yukawa parameters. A given string-derived sector then predicts low-energy slopes. Its gauge kinetic functions, matter-metric or Yukawa slopes, source charge, scalar trajectory, and scalar range determine a Damour--Donoghue weak-equivalence-principle (WEP) vector and a clock-drift vector. The fit assumes one long-range scalar or an aligned multi-field direction. With that assumption, WEP tests and secular clock drifts probe related projections of the same scalar-slope vector. The minimal two-charge Damour--Donoghue fit uses Ti--Pt MICROSCOPE, Be--Ti torsion-balance, and $^{85}$Rb--$^{87}$Rb atom-interferometer data, then adds the Yb$^+$ E3/E2 secular $\alpha$-drift row. The WEP-only fit gives $D_{\hat m}=(-6.06\pm34.91)\times10^{-12}$ and $D_e=(8.80\pm46.46)\times10^{-12}$, with correlation $-0.99958$. The clock input is $\dot\alpha/\alpha=1.0(1.1)\times10^{-18}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. It matches the WEP marginal reach when $|\zeta|=2.37\times10^{-8}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, with $\zeta=\dot\varphi/\alpha_E$. For the benchmark $\dot\varphi=\xi H_0$ and $\alpha_E=10^{-3}\alpha_0$, this gives $\xi/\alpha_0\simeq0.34$. A model becomes testable after it supplies $r=D_{\hat m}/D_e$, the scalar amplitude, and $\zeta$. The Damour--Piazza--Veneziano runaway-dilaton estimate lies near $\eta\sim10^{-12}$ for order-unity $n=2$ parameters, well above the MICROSCOPE-level WEP scale. In the representative-isotope two-charge model, a MICROSCOPE-level Be--Ti-like row would reduce the long WEP axis by a factor $27.8$; a repeated Ti--Pt-like row would barely change it. The calculation tests compactification-level predictions for string-derived dilaton or modulus sectors after the model supplies its low-energy data.
authors: Ahmed Farag Ali

papers.title: Bayesian Inference in Partially Observed Critical Systems
papers.abstract: We ask how much of a large random system must be observed before a global average can be inferred with controlled uncertainty. For the random transposition shuffle, a conjugate Bayesian estimator of the average displacement, computed from $m$ uniformly sampled cards, has relative uncertainty $1/\sqrt{2m}$, independent of the deck size $n$. The law of total variance exposes a second error, the floor $R_n$, which arises because the observed configuration is a single draw from equilibrium: no relative tolerance below $\kappa\sqrt{R_n}$ can be certified, even by a census. For the shuffle we derive $R_n=(2n^2+7)/\bigl(5(n-1)^2(n+1)\bigr)$ and show that the posterior remains calibrated. At the critical point of the two-dimensional Ising model the floor of the energy vanishes, whereas that of the magnetisation stays near $0.072$; its mean-field limit is $\sqrt{2}-1$. For correlated fields read by sensor networks, the usual 95\% interval covers the ensemble mean in 7\% of cases. Bounding the floor from one realisation, as in single-chain Monte Carlo diagnostics, requires an assumption on the decay of correlations.
authors: Mihika Singhania

papers.title: Cutting, Shuffling and Diffusion as a Coarsening Process
papers.abstract: Cutting and shuffling (CS) rearranges fluid without stretching, but homogenisation requires diffusion (D); this interaction is not well understood. We show that CSD is a coarsening process, with scale $\bar\ell=L(n_c\mathrm{Pe}/2)^{-1/3}$ rather than the Batchelor scale, and that cutting acts as a fractional Laplacian in wavenumber, giving the exact mixing rate $\gamma=2^{1/3}|a_1'|n_c^{2/3}\lambda\mathrm{Pe}^{-1/3}$ for $n_c$ cuts per event at rate $\lambda$, with $a_1'=-1.0188\dots$ the first zero of $\mathrm{Ai}'$. This holds in any dimension for random and deterministic protocols, extends to finite-time mixing, and places CSD in a known non-equilibrium universality class.
authors: Daniel Lester, Tanguy LeBorgne, Joris Heyman

papers.title: Amorphization-Depth-Dependent Bismuth Redistribution and Activation in Silicon for Quantum Devices
papers.abstract: Near-surface bismuth donors are promising for silicon quantum devices because of their rich electron-nuclear spin structure and long spin coherence, but their electrical activation is strongly influenced by implantation-induced amorphization. We compare redistribution and electrical activation of 20 keV Bi implanted directly into Si and after Si preamorphization. The two routes produce amorphous-layer depths of approximately 47 nm and 177 +/- 15 nm, respectively. After annealing at 650 C for 300 s, Rutherford backscattering spectrometry and channeling reveal comparable substitutional Bi fractions of 91 +/- 2% and 89 +/- 4%, whereas Hall measurements indicate Hall-derived electrical activation yields of approximately 60% and 90%, respectively. Depth-resolved ion-scattering analysis reveals a buried Bi-related feature at or beyond the initial amorphous/crystalline interface, within the end-of-range region, together with increasing surface segregation at higher annealing temperatures. The buried feature is consistent with trapping near residual end-of-range defects. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and low-temperature photoluminescence on the Bi-only sample reveal no resolvable Bi-oxide contribution and a donor-related optical signature, respectively. These results show that amorphization depth and regrowth geometry govern Bi redistribution and influence electrical activation beyond substitutional incorporation alone.
authors: Youcef A. Bioud, Simon-Jean Michel, Sebastien Francoeur, Sjoerd Roorda, Eva Dupont-Ferrier

papers.title: Evaluation of a Double Integral with Exponentials and Two Generalized Laguerre Polynomials and Its Associated Moments
papers.abstract: We analytically evaluate in terms of finite sums, the following definite improper integral, which appears in the quantum field theoretical calculation involving elementary charged particles having charge $\pm e$ in presence of a constant external magnetic field $\mathbf{B}=B\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ $$ I_{abln}^{\mu_1\dots\mu_r}(\mathbf{q}_\perp,|eB|) = \int\!\!\dfrac{d^2k_\perp}{(2\pi)^2}k_\perp^{\mu_1} \dots k_\perp^{\mu_r} \exp \bigg(-\frac{\mathbf{k}_\perp^2+\mathbf{p}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg) L^a_l \bigg(\frac{2\mathbf{k}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg) L^b_n \bigg(\frac{2\mathbf{p}_\perp^2}{|eB|}\bigg)\bigg|_{\mathbf{p}_\perp=(\mathbf{q}_\perp+\mathbf{k}_\perp)} $$ where $\mu_i \in \{1,2\}$, $l\ge 0$, $n\ge 0$ and $L_l^a(x)$ are the generalized Laguerre polynomials. We also provide explicit expressions of the result up to the fourth moment i.e. $r=4$, which are sufficient for most of the field theoretical calculations.
authors: Snigdha Ghosh

papers.title: Formation and Charge Relaxation of Julia-Zee Dyons in Classical Lattice Simulations
papers.abstract: We demonstrate the formation and subsequent evolution of Julia--Zee dyons in $(3+1)$-dimensional classical lattice simulations of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)\to\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry-breaking model in an expanding background. The gauge and Higgs fields are prepared thermally, subjected to an ultraviolet filter, and evolved through a mass quench and subsequent expansion. Classical dyons can carry continuous electric charge, and we find charge magnitudes exceeding four times the electric charge unit $g$. Their measured electric-charge magnitudes tend to decrease during the subsequent evolution, consistent with charge exchange with the surrounding fields. At late times, the magnetic monopoles persist while the number of dyons and their observed charge range decrease, with only a few identified dyons remaining at the end of the simulations.
authors: Masaki Yamada

papers.title: The Art of Orbifolding by Huge Non-Abelian Groups
papers.abstract: We compute torus partition functions of orbifolds of two-dimensional chiral fermions by huge non-Abelian groups involving the Conway group, one of the sporadic finite simple groups. This seemingly standard problem turns out to contain, somewhat unexpectedly, multiple major issues hitherto unresolved, both at the level of the principle and at the level of practice. We describe in detail how they can be overcome. Although the methods described in this paper are generally applicable, the choice of the particular orbifolds we consider in this paper was motivated by the search for the periodicity element of topological modular forms. We will provide a brief introduction to this question, to explain why all the techniques in this paper had to be developed. Unfortunately, the orbifolds we considered turned out not to be the periodicity element.
authors: Jan Albert, Masaki Okada, Yuji Tachikawa

papers.title: Instanton Structure from 325-Loop 3D $\phi^3$ Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: The high order behavior of perturbation theory provides insight into non-perturbative phenomenon in quantum field theory. While extensively studied in simplified models, high order behavior is challenging to access in more realistic field theories due to the complexity of the standard Feynman diagrammatic expansion. Building on recent progress in global sampling on the moduli space of tropical curves, we introduce an annealed importance sampling framework for tropical field theory. Our approach overcomes the exponential weight-variance barrier, allowing precise numerical calculations to high orders. We apply our technique to compute the perturbative series for the two-point function in the massive three-dimensional $\phi^3$ theory through 325 loops. These coefficients determine the instanton action in $\phi^3$ theory to 0.03\% precision, confirm the collective-coordinate exponent, and extract the one-loop determinant and the instanton fluctuation corrections through four loops, in remarkable agreement with direct semiclassical calculations. Our approach is applicable to a variety of related field theories, facilitating the quantitative exploration of their high loop behavior.
authors: Ian Moult, Bo Wang

papers.title: A Correspondence Between Qubit- and Boson-Based Sensing Protocols
papers.abstract: Recent years have seen a surge of interest in adapting non-classical states to search for physics beyond the Standard Model, including both qubit- and boson-based systems. These two classes of systems are closely related through the Holstein--Primakoff transformation (HPT). In this work, we show that the HPT offers novel insights into inherently quantum-mechanical detection of new physics. We begin by discussing how the HPT can be used to unify certain existing qubit- and boson-based proposals in a single framework. We then show how it naturally reveals a novel generalization of GHZ states which offer superior performance for the detection of rare interactions. We demonstrate that these novel states can be readily prepared, and combine the coherent advantage of GHZ states with superior error rejection. Finally, we show that the HPT also reveals a natural extension of the Hamiltonian-Not-in-Lindblad-Span theorem for collections of bosonic modes.
authors: Zachary Bogorad, Roni Harnik

papers.title: Cusp regularization with spin structures and gravitational anomalies
papers.abstract: The family of $SL(2,\mathbb Z)$ black holes has an accumulation point corresponding to a cusped geometry, which causes the sum over black holes to diverge. We extend cusp regularization to the sum over geometries compatible with a fixed boundary spin structure. For $c_L=c_R$, including the cusp as a counterterm cancels the leading divergence for each of the three even boundary spin structures. The required subtraction is the same in all three sectors and is two thirds of the bosonic one. We further show that gravitational anomalies cause cancellations between black hole contributions, removing the leading cusp divergence except at $c_L-c_R=0,\pm24$ in pure gravity and $c_L-c_R=0,\pm12$ in $\mathcal N=(1,1)$ supergravity. We also derive the spin structure dependent anomaly phases responsible for these cancellations.
authors: Elisa Tabor, Cynthia Yan

papers.title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
papers.abstract: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^\omega(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $\omega\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,\gamma,\epsilon)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $\omega_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $\omega$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD
authors: Alison Warman

papers.title: Analytic Bootstrap Solution for Quantum Mechanics on a Circle
papers.abstract: We solve the Schr\"odinger equation for a particle in the circle with a quantum mechanical bootstrap method. The main idea is that in physical situations one needs solutions of the recursion relations for the Fourier coefficients of the measure that vanish exponentially fast. We show that this results in a (generalized) continued fraction representation of the solution. The solution is an analytical function of the couplings and the energy. We also show how one this method directly computes the density of states and checking that the answer is physical is reduced to checking an inequality for a single variable. We also show how to reconstruct the wave function and how to extract the quasimomentum of the particle as a function of the energy. We illustrate our solution in the simplest case of the Mathieu equation, where we show that the method can easily resolve exponentially small bands in the band spectrum.
authors: David Berenstein, Upamanyu Moitra

papers.title: Cosmology of the Baby Universe in Coupled SYK
papers.abstract: We analyze the structure of the baby universe which arises in the coupled SYK realization of the AS$^2$ geometry. To do this, we develop and leverage combinatorial arguments about traces of many Majoranas which remain valid at finite $N$ and $p$ and thus furnish the finite $\lambda$ completion of the chord rules found in [1]. We find that there is a first order phase transition which persists in the $\beta\rightarrow\infty$ limit between the thermal AdS and AS$^2$ phases parameterized by the mass of the heavy particle insertion and the ratio between the SYK and Maldacena-Qi coupling constants. We then explore Lorentzian time evolution in the baby universe and find a cosine scale factor confirming the big bang / big crunch nature of the bulk cosmology.
authors: Andrew Sontag

papers.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
papers.abstract: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states, which concentrate at a particular $R$-charge. This division has a precise mathematical meaning as two different types of cohomologies of the Higgs branch target space. We argue that a natural probe of BPS chaos in these models is the Berry/Chern curvature. In the case of the Gepner model, we use localization techniques in an auxiliary two-dimensional CFT to compute the curvature, its RMT properties, and deviations from it.
authors: Micha Berkooz, Trivko Kukolj, Ohad Mamroud, Josef Seitz

papers.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
papers.abstract: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.
authors: Yulia A. Ageeva, Andrey K. Sharofeev

papers.title: Semi-agnostic inspiral modeling: the massless scalar case at leading post-Newtonian order
papers.abstract: We introduce a semi-agnostic modeling framework for black hole binary inspirals beyond general relativity that fixes the field content without selecting a particular theory. We expand in the post-Newtonian order and in powers of $l/L$, where $l$ is the characteristic length-scale that controls deviations from General Relativity and $L$ is the characteristic length-scale of the system. We focus on the case of a massless scalar field coupled with the metric, at leading post-Newtonian order. Taking into account the scaling with $l/L$ of both the interaction terms and the quantities that characterise the sources, we find that the inspiral can be described in terms of a small number of universal parameters. Such a parametrisation is suitable for obtaining combined bounds from multiple sources and performing searches for specific fields.
authors: Dario Rossi, Leonardo Gualtieri, Thomas P. Sotiriou

papers.title: Phase Transitions in Mismatched Bayesian Inference for the Ising Model
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference with a mismatched model can develop an overconfident phase, characterized by posterior agreement without faithful reconstruction of the true state. We study Bayesian inference from noisy bond measurements of an Ising model in its paramagnetic phase, with true inverse temperature $\beta$ and measurement-noise strength $\Delta$, while inference assumes corresponding parameters $\beta_Q$ and $\Delta_Q$. Using replica field theory, we analytically show that the overconfidence phase can occur when inference underestimates the measurement noise ($\Delta_Q < \Delta$) or assumes a lower prior temperature than the true one ($\beta_Q > \beta$). An exact change of variables maps the problem to a correlated random-bond Ising model, where the informative, uninformative, and overconfident phases correspond to ferromagnetic, paramagnetic, and spin-glass phases, respectively. We further perform Monte Carlo simulations of the mapped model in three dimensions and establish a finite overconfident region between the informative and uninformative phases, consistent with our analytical prediction. Finally, we show that the true model parameters can be inferred directly from the measurement records, providing a natural route to calibrating the inference model.
authors: Xinyu Sun, Zhou-Quan Wan, Shao-Kai Jian, Hong Yao

papers.title: An open EFT for dark matter searches with matter-wave interferometers
papers.abstract: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) are a genuine quantum probe of dark matter (DM), being sensitive to DM-induced phase shifts and loss of contrast. Treating the interferometer as an open quantum system and the dark sector as its environment, we derive an open EFT to study these signatures using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Starting from a microscopic theory, we derive the interferometer's effective action, which we then project onto the many-body worldline sectors relevant for atom interferometers and MWIs employing mesoscopic objects, i.e., composite-particle interferometers (CPIs). This construction clarifies the heavy-probe limit and organizes phase shifts and decoherence as distinct real-time components of the influence action: the retarded kernel controls the causal response of the environment, while the Keldysh kernel controls environmental fluctuations and hence loss of contrast. At leading order, these kernels reduce to: (i) DM bubble diagrams in the case of four-point interactions, and (ii) dressed in-medium mediator propagators in the case of long-range interactions, where the dressing is provided by the DM environment. Within this framework, we study the signatures of elastic spin-independent sub-GeV DM scattering off nucleons and find that: (i) owing to Bose enhancements below the DM wave-particle boundary, ambitious CPIs could probe Higgs-portal DM with mass below 1 eV in an unexplored region of model space; (ii) for DM coupled to nucleons via a light hadrophilic scalar, the DM background can drive the mediator's in-medium mass tachyonic over much of parameter space; outside these regions, CPIs could probe provide powerful probes of light DM.
authors: Leonardo Badurina, Kathryn M. Zurek

papers.title: Local Measures in Odd de Sitter
papers.abstract: We show that massless theories in odd-dimensional de Sitter space have very simple measures---the modulus squared of the late-time wavefunctional---at tree level. They are local functionals; in particular, all wavefunction coefficients vanish at separated positions. All the usual singularities of nonlocal wavefunctions in even dimensions only affect the phase in the odd dimensional case. Hence a closed formula can be written for any number of points. We focus on three examples: the non-linear sigma model, Yang-Mills theory and General Relativity, from dimensions three to seven.
authors: Guilherme L. Pimentel, Nicole Righi, Behrang Tafreshi

papers.title: Symmetry-resolved fermionic correlations in iron-oxide ground spaces
papers.abstract: Symmetries of quantum systems provide a natural way to organize the eigenspaces of many-body Hamiltonians. When degeneracies exist, however, they play a more subtle role as different sets of symmetry operators can resolve the same energy subspace into states with very different correlation properties. We study this interplay using a sequence of FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ models. For a Hubbard model of FeO, the ground space is 16-fold degenerate. Resolving it by local magnetizations gives a basis of Slater determinants, while total-spin quantum numbers select entangled and non-Gaussian states from the same ground manifold. Adding density-density Hund interactions breaks the independent spin rotations and reduces the ground space to a spin-reversal pair with maximal magnetization. These states are extremely close to Slater determinants in their natural occupations, yet have finite two-body cumulants and conserved-operator algebras whose orbit dimensions differ substantially from the Slater values. Fe$_2$O$_2$ provides a larger example in which spatial mode entanglement can be substantial while fermionic non-Gaussianity remains weak, with the conserved-operator structure again distinguishing the state from the corresponding Slater transformation class. Together, these examples show that symmetry resolution, mode entanglement, reduced-density-matrix correlations, and conserved-operator structure provide complementary information about interacting and degenerate electronic ground states.
authors: Federico Petrovich, Daniel Staros, Daniel N. Blaschke, Jian-Xin Zhu, M. Cerezo

papers.title: Typicality of entanglement growth and transport fluctuations in quantum symmetric exclusion processes
papers.abstract: We use macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to establish the typicality of charge-transfer statistics and entanglement dynamics in the quantum symmetric exclusion process, a model of stochastically hopping free fermions with diffusive transport and long-range quantum coherence. We show that the leading long-time charge-transfer full counting statistics of individual noise realizations coincide almost surely with those of the classical symmetric exclusion process (SSEP), in equilibrium and following quenches from arbitrary occupation-diagonal product states. Our results apply to transient fluctuations in the thermodynamic limit, extending previous work that has primarily focused on stationary regimes. Our approach compares the noise averages of the charge-transfer generating function and its inverse. The former reduces to SSEP, while the latter maps to an auxiliary Brownian energy process whose MFT saddle-point problem is related to that of SSEP, yielding matching large-deviation exponents. Through free-fermion identities relating entanglement to subsystem-number fluctuations, this establishes the self-averaging of the covariance-matrix eigenvalue distribution and of R\'enyi and von Neumann entropies. We obtain asymptotically exact predictions for entanglement growth from domain-wall and N\'eel initial states, in excellent agreement with numerical simulations.
authors: Ewan McCulloch

papers.title: Dark Matter Coherent Freeze-Out Mechanism: A Comprehensive Analysis
papers.abstract: Both Weakly-Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP) and Axion-Like Particle (ALP) are attractive particle dark matter candidates. In this paper we consider a scenario in which both WIMP and ALP are present. The two species interact via a non-derivative quadratic coupling modeled on the axion-nucleon interaction in QCD. We show that even a small (Planck-suppressed) coupling can drastically modify the cosmological history of both species. In the very early Universe, the ALP field acquires a vacuum expectation value, and the system undergoes an inverse phase transition at a temperature around or below the weak scale. WIMPs may remain in equilibrium far beyond the usual freeze-out time, eventually decoupling via a novel "coherent freeze-out" mechanism. WIMP annihilation cross sections several orders of magnitude above the canonical thermal target value can be consistent with the observed relic density in the coherent freeze-out scenario. At the same time, coherent oscillations of the ALP field do not begin until after the phase transition, and the initial conditions for these oscillations are set by the thermal physics of the phase transition. The ALP relic density is then predicted unambiguously in terms of the WIMP mass and coupling. We term this scenario "ALP miracle", since the observed relic density is obtained when these parameters are around their natural values, the weak and the Planck scale. The ALP miracle scenario prefers the ALP mass above about $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}$, far larger than other popular ALP dark matter models. The ALP miracle parameter space overlaps with a currently allowed region of the QCD axion band, a large fraction of which is expected to be probed by the proposed IAXO experiment.
authors: Steven Ferrante, Lillian Luo, Maxim Perelstein, Bingrong Yu

papers.title: The Harmonic Structure of Multiparticle Scattering: Amplitude Projection and Non-Renormalization
papers.abstract: We develop a projection formalism for four-dimensional massless scattering amplitudes based on the construction of harmonics on multi-particle phase space. This provides a generalization of the partial-wave decomposition valid for any number of particles. Applying this formalism to calculations of on-shell cuts, we show that any cut calculation can be rewritten as a sum of products of projected coefficients and derive a condition for this sum to vanish. Using the on-shell renormalization group equation in combination with our projection formalism, we derive new non-renormalization theorems for effective field theories valid at general loop orders.
authors: Nathaniel Craig, Brian Henning, Michael Stadlbauer

papers.title: Mesons, Confinement, and Complexity: A Krylov Space Perspective on the Long-Range Ising Chain
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between confinement and Krylov complexity in the long-range transverse-field Ising chain, where power-law interactions $\sim 1/r^{\alpha}$ generate an effective confining potential between domain walls without an explicit symmetry-breaking field. Using the time-averaged Krylov state complexity after a quench as a diagnostic, we find that the complexity is strongly suppressed and only weakly system size-dependent at small $\alpha$ and small transverse field $h_x$, where confinement is strongest, and crosses over to rapid growth at larger $\alpha$, where it increases with system size. Within the confined regime, the oscillation frequencies of the complexity agree with the meson masses of an effective two-kink model, with the dominant frequency growing linearly with the lightest meson mass and the time-averaged complexity decreasing approximately as its inverse square. We further study operator Krylov complexity at finite temperature using the Wightman inner product. At low temperature, it exhibits bounded oscillations that directly encode the meson spectrum, whereas this structure is progressively washed out as the temperature increases. These results identify Krylov complexity as a spectroscopic probe of interaction-induced confinement and reproduce, in a microscopic lattice model, the hallmarks of Krylov complexity identified in confining field theories.
authors: Xuhao Jiang, Jad C. Halimeh, N. S. Srivatsa

papers.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
papers.abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.
authors: Suzanne Bintanja, Amey P. Gaikwad, Dikshant Rathore

papers.title: Universal Scaling of Conditional Mutual Information in Classical Stochastic Dynamics
papers.abstract: Conditional mutual information (CMI) characterizes dependence between two regions conditioned on an intervening buffer. Its characteristic decay length, the Markov length, has recently been identified as a diverging length scale at mixed-state phase transitions. Here, we investigate CMI dynamics in one-dimensional classical stochastic models and propose a universal scaling form for systems whose Markov length diverges with time. We derive this form in the inactive phase of parity-conserving directed percolation, where domain-wall coarsening generates a growing length scale and a self-similar probability distribution. We introduce a Hankel-based truncation scheme that enables matrix-product-state simulations at long times and over large spatial regions. Using this method, we verify the proposed scaling both in the inactive phase and at the nonequilibrium critical point, where the dynamical critical exponent governs Markov-length growth. More broadly, the same scaling form captures cases in which collective inference sets the diverging Markov length. Despite these distinct mechanisms, the CMI between fixed microscopic regions exhibits a common scaling dimension of two. Finally, we extend this framework to temporal CMI, establishing an analogous relation between the strength of conditional dependence in time domain and its characteristic memory time.
authors: Songlei Wang, Chenguang Liang, Zhi-Cheng Yang

papers.title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
papers.abstract: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.
authors: Junheng Tao, Paige Robichaud, Christian Hallas, Giseok Lee, John M. Doyle

papers.title: Axionic Quintessence in Heterotic String Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate axionic quintessence in heterotic string compactifications. Starting from the ten-dimensional theory, we derive the four-dimensional axion effective action, including gauge couplings and non-perturbative potentials, and identify the curvature terms that can correct it. We examine the geometric requirements for ultralight axions generated by exponentially suppressed worldsheet instantons, finding significant restrictions through an exploratory scan of toric Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces. In an illustrative K3-fibred setup, the minimal benchmark also encounters a tension with the positivity of the one-loop corrected gauge kinetic functions. Aligned worldsheet-instanton contributions provide a way to alleviate this tension and yield an ultralight axion with a phenomenologically relevant decay constant. Our analysis also identifies lower-action instantons whose contributions must be controlled to preserve the ultralight axion. We then study the resulting class of quintessence potentials and qualitatively compare their late-time cosmological solutions with observationally preferred ranges.
authors: David Andriot, Margherita Putti, Leo Veissiere

papers.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems
papers.abstract: Open quantum systems can display metastability, with multiple long-lived states coexisting. Examples include the bistability of bright and dim manifolds in nonlinear driven resonators, or the long-lived coherent states of opposite phases in parametrically-driven systems, the building block of cat-state-based quantum computers. Metastability often emerges at system sizes where density-matrix evolution is impractical. Quantum trajectories mitigate this issue by evolving wavefunctions rather than density matrices. Metastable states then emerge as attractors towards which the system rapidly relaxes until a rare switching event brings it to another attractor. Simulating them remains costly, as one must resolve fast intra-attractor dynamics over timescales long enough to gather switching statistics. To tackle this problem, we introduce the Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling (DiSLOU) method, which combines three optimization layers: (i) Switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize the number of quantum jumps in each metastable region. (ii) Diagonal propagation: the no-jump evolution is accelerated by diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian once per attractor. (iii) Local reduced eigenspaces: the no-jump state can be faithfully propagated in a truncated subspace of only slowly decaying eigenmodes. We benchmark DiSLOU on the driven-dissipative Kerr resonator, finding no measurable loss of accuracy and the largest speedup in the bistable regime, where standard trajectories are most expensive. We then apply the method to the more challenging problem of accurately simulating rare bit-flip events in the cat manifold emerging in a two-mode dissipatively stabilized parametric oscillator, obtaining a performance improvement of over one order of magnitude. An implementation of DiSLOU in Julia is available as an open-source package.
authors: Pietro Pacchioni, Alberto Mercurio, Patrick Winkel, Fabrizio Minganti

papers.title: Equilibrium Learning of Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Equilibrium learning trains a physical system using observables of its relaxed states. We extend this principle to gate-based quantum circuits by embedding a parametrized circuit in a Feynman-Kitaev (FK) Hamiltonian and imposing the compilation target either through an output clamping term or through a target-dependent cyclic condition on the clock register. The ground state energies and the overlaps of the corresponding ground states with the free history state define faithful cost functions for unitary and state compilation. We show that these costs are nonlinear functions of the compilation infidelity and therefore reshape the optimization landscape. We show that starting from the free history state, quantum phase estimation can prepare the relevant ground states and estimate the cost functions with polynomial resources. In two-qubit benchmarks, optimization with the equilibrium cost functions reaches a fixed fidelity threshold in fewer sweeps than standard compilation infidelity cost function for many instances. The results demonstrate the potential for encoding quantum learning problems as computation of equilibrium observables.
authors: Frank Barrows, Touheed Atif, Yi\u{g}it Suba\c{s}\i, Tyler Volkoff

papers.title: An algebraic characterisation of $n$-qubit pure-state invariants
papers.abstract: We study the set of $n$-qubit pure quantum states. Specifically, we consider their incarnation as density matrices in Bloch representation. Building on prior work, we define a family of quadratic functions in Pauli expectation values, and fully characterise all instances that result in state-independent purity constraints. The resulting family of pure-state invariants is surprisingly rich in structure, with strong ties to the geometry of symplectic polar spaces. After charting the general landscape, we define a sub-family of pure-state invariants that satisfies the dynamical constraint of being stable under state update. We prove that it corresponds with (different embeddings of) symplectic Lie algebras $\mathfrak{sp}(2^{n-1})\subset\mathfrak{su}(2^n)$, which admit a generating set of Pauli operators. We carefully distinguish the symplectic case from its orthogonal counterpart, using the Arf invariant of quadratic refinements of the symplectic form on the projective Pauli group, which we further identify with quaternionic structures on $\mathbb{C}^{2^n}$ that are both generated by and restricted to Pauli operators. As a consequence of this analysis, we reveal previously largely overlooked structure in the $n$-qubit Pauli group. We highlight this in a number of examples. We characterise all state-independent uncertainty relations in variance for Pauli observables, as well as all Pauli channels for which the output fidelity and output purity are state-independent. We further show that the orbits of the projective stabiliser groups of pure-state invariants, which for $n\geq2$ are proper subgroups of the Clifford group, form complex projective state $2$-designs, while their unitary lifts form symplectic $2$-designs.
authors: Markus Frembs

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Schwinger effect in an imaginary magnetic field
papers.abstract: We investigate a non-Hermitian Schwinger effect by analyzing a one-loop effective Lagrangian of scalar and Dirac quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the presence of a real electric field and a parallel imaginary magnetic field. We show that an imaginary magnetic field produces an additional pole family in the integrand of the proper-time representation. Unlike a real magnetic field, an imaginary magnetic field can generate a nonzero imaginary part of the effective Lagrangian even in the absence of an electric field. The interplay between the two fields leads to nontrivial phenomena, such as a cancellation mechanism between the contributions of two fields. We also point out that when the ratio of two field strengths is rational, some poles among the two families coincide, and a careful treatment of double poles is required. By further examining the complex Landau-level structure of the electric-pole contribution, we find that the field dependence of the vacuum decay rate from each Landau level exhibits a sinusoidal-like behavior, and their sum determines the overall field dependence. Our results clarify the analytic structure of the QED effective Lagrangian in imaginary magnetic backgrounds and provide a basis for investigating its relation to non-Hermitian phenomena in the QED vacuum.
authors: Ahmad Jafar Arifi, Kei Suzuki

papers.title: Custodial scalars and Higgs branch
papers.abstract: We show that, for most gauged scalar fields, the scalar potential can be systematically organised into an ordered tree of increasingly symmetric operators. The intermediary global symmetries represented in the tree allow at tree-level a subset of the scalar field components, the custodial scalars, to be technically lighter than the scalar mass scale, or even exactly massless (so-called accidents). We further demonstrate, using the notion of moment maps, that such structure can be related to the Higgs branch of supersymmetric theories, allowing the use of powerful symplectic geometry tools in studying the vacuum of non-supersymmetric scalar potentials. We present various applications, from an example of a non-abelian accident to a Standard Model-like Higgs sector generated from custodial scalars.
authors: Luc Darm\'e, Baptiste Filoche, Sebastian Monath

papers.title: Hironaka decompositions in supersymmetric theories: an exploration
papers.abstract: We ask when tree-level supersymmetric cohomology admits a Hironaka decomposition: a unique expansion in finitely many secondary operators with polynomial coefficients in algebraically independent bosonic primaries. Such a decomposition organizes the cohomology into towers with a common set of unrestricted dressings. For diagonal models with $N$ labels, $d\geq1$ bosonic species and $f$ fermionic species, we construct this decomposition and obtain $(N!)^{d-1}2^{fN}$ secondaries. We also prove that the scalar-branch ring of ABJM theory admits a Hironaka decomposition at every rank and positive integer Chern--Simons level, and construct explicit bases for the $SU(2)\times SU(2)$ Klebanov--Witten scalar ring. We also do the same for the Higgs branches of two class-S theories. However, not all supersymmetric cohomologies admit a Hironaka decomposition. In the Wess--Zumino model with $W=x^2y^2$, every positive-degree scalar annihilates the nonzero class $xy$, while $x^n$ is in cohomology for every $n\geq 1$. These two properties rule out a Hironaka decomposition over scalar primaries.
authors: Abhijit Gadde, Rajat Raj, Shivansh Tomar

papers.title: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking
papers.abstract: Grokking is a delayed transition from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks (NNs). We examine whether scaling and renormalization group (RG) theories can describe this dynamics, establishing a quantitative physical framework for neural generalization transitions. For modular addition on a two-layer NN, an ensemble of trained models defines an order parameter (the squared weight norm) and fluctuation proxies for the heat capacity and the susceptibility, with training epoch and weight decay serving as thermal and field control coordinates. To bridge neural architectures to real-space RG, we construct an exact coupling matrix via a second-order expansion of the loss with respect to per-neuron norms and use its Fiedler vector to define an effective geometry. This spectral ordering yields a monotonic spatial decay of coupling strength that is absent under random permutations. We then execute real-space RG by block-spin aggregating adjacent neurons and parameterizing the coupling matrix into off-diagonal band strengths. Linearizing this local RG map yields relevant scaling exponents and five derived critical exponents, with direct empirical estimates matching RG predictions within 1-10%. Overall, our framework provides a consistent effective description of grokking, suggesting the scaling and renormalization group formalism as a tool to investigate NN dynamics.
authors: Min Chen, Junqi Wang, Zeguan Wu, Wenhao Huang, Junyu Liu

papers.title: Ensemble-dependent condensate statistics and correlations in an ideal Bose gas
papers.abstract: The choice of statistical ensemble has a measurable impact on the statistical description of Bose-Einstein condensates beyond the well-known grand canonical anomaly. We develop a segmented-contour approach for the ideal Bose gas, which refines the saddle-point approximation by including non-Gaussian corrections in the canonical and microcanonical ensembles. The method applies to a broad class of noninteracting spectra, and provides efficient access to condensate fluctuations, higher moments, and correlation functions. For a three-dimensional harmonic trap with fixed anisotropy, we find that the ratio of the maxima of the microcanonical and canonical condensate-number variances approaches the theoretically predicted asymptotic value $1-3\zeta(3)^2/[4\zeta(2)\zeta(4)]\approx 0.391$ only extremely slowly with increasing particle number. We also show that ensemble effects are visible in the second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(x)$ near the condensation crossover. After ballistic release from a three-dimensional harmonic trap, the time evolution of $g^{(2)}(x)$ preserves the differences between statistical ensembles.
authors: Szymon Augustynowicz, Jan Oko\'nski, Maciej B. Kruk, Ilja Zebergs, Jan Joachim Arlt, Kazimierz Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Krzysztof Paw{\l}owski

papers.title: Landau singularity of the K3 maximal cut in black-hole scattering at fifth post-Minkowskian order
papers.abstract: Modeling the gravitational waves from merging black holes requires precise calculations of the two-body problem. The post-Minkowskian expansion of black-hole scattering, in powers of Newton's constant, now stands at fifth order, four loops. At this order one part of the deflection diverges when the black holes pass at about 94 percent of the speed of light. The divergence is known to come from periods of a K3 surface, which has a node at this speed. We show that the node lies on the integration contour of the K3 maximal cut, which makes this speed a Landau singularity of the cut. Requiring the divergence to cancel, without introducing new infinities, has been shown to fix the memory contribution, named for the permanent displacement that the waves leave in test masses, up to one constant. We derive the leading coefficients of its boundary integrals in closed form. We obtain both results from maximal cuts and boundary limits, without an integration-by-parts reduction of the full four-loop integrand. We also continue the K3 and Calabi--Yau periods of these integrals to the energies of bound orbits, as in the inspiral before a merger.
authors: Matthew D. Schwartz

papers.title: Universal Critical Jump for Inverse-Square Ising Ferromagnets
papers.abstract: For every translation-invariant ferromagnetic Ising chain with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, we prove $2\beta_cBm_c^2=1$, without restrictions on the finite core or the tail convergence rate. The proof bounds the energy of macroscopic interfaces and rules them out if the critical product exceeds one. Despite the nonzero jump, connected susceptibility is infinite both at criticality and in a neighboring ordered interval. At the critical coupling, the excess magnetization decays more slowly than any positive power of the field as the field tends to zero. We also prove the jump relation in continuous time, for a positive-Stieltjes class of Ohmic spin-boson models.
authors: Dyuman Bhattacharya

papers.title: Many-body entanglement quantification in arbitrary states through a few partial-transpose moments
papers.abstract: Can the entanglement of an arbitrary many-body state be quantified without reconstructing the state? We answer the question affirmatively by showing how the measure of logarithmic negativity can be estimated using a finite number of even partial transpose (PT) moments of a many-body state. Considering the squared PT spectrum as a probability measure, we solve exactly the task of a truncated Hausdorff moment problem with Gauss and Gauss-Radau quadrature. We obtain a hierarchy of lower bounds on the logarithmic negativity, which improves with increasing order of moments. Convergence to the exact value of the measure can be achieved for every state of finite dimension. We illustrate the bounds for ground states of three different interacting spin models, as well as for a thermal state. An error analysis demonstrates the efficacy of our scheme towards handling the limitation of finite statistics encountered in actual experiments with randomized measurements. Moreover, an example of density matrix renormalization group based numerical estimation is provided for handling system sizes beyond the scope of exact diagonalization.
authors: Sudip Chakrabarty, A. S. Majumdar

papers.title: Analog Quantum Experiments Meet Automatic Differentiation - from Programs to Atoms
papers.abstract: Gradient-based optimization of analog quantum hardware poses a concrete programming problem: given an executable experiment P(\theta) that returns only measurement samples, what executable experiment should the system run to obtain (d/d\theta_ell)P(\theta)? Conventional automatic differentiation cannot propagate through the inaccessible quantum state, while finite differences require a noise-sensitive step size and analytic gradient identities cover only parts of an experiment. We present DiffSimuQ, which shows that a broad class of open-loop analog quantum experiments is closed under automatic differentiation. A compositional transformation maps P(\theta) to a derivative program D_ell[P(\theta)] in the same language whose expected outcome is exactly the derivative. Only continuous evolution requires a strategy-specific rule, and we give two realizations. Our Nyquist shift rule (NSR) applies to general time-dependent evolution: we prove that the observable response to shifting the Hamiltonian along its tangent is band-limited even for non-commuting controls, enabling exact reconstruction from shifted executions. For involutory generators, a parameter-shift realization (PSR) inserts a parameter-independent operation at a sampled time. Because derivative programs remain ordinary programs, source and derivative experiments share one compiler, which reuses the source realization, lowers branches to device-ready neutral-atom controls, and selects between NSR and PSR based on estimated cost. Under device noise, the exact derivative programs differentiate the objective realized by the device, with hardware realization errors treated separately. In machine-level noisy emulation, NSR and PSR avoid the finite-difference error floor and improve closed-loop optimization; they win in complementary cost regimes, while each derivative branch at 1000 qubits add at most 0.3% to source compilation time.
authors: Yue Shi, Pengyu Liu, Yuxiang Peng

papers.title: Quantum circuit simulation with high-order optical tensor processing
papers.abstract: Classical simulation is essential for developing and testing quantum circuits, but the exponential growth of Hilbert space challenges conventional digital processors. Here, we introduce a classical optical quantum simulation architecture that treats gates and batches of input states as independent tensor dimensions rather than separate simulation instances, while mapping eligible tensor network contractions onto the same processor. Using co-designed multidimensional encoding and readout across spatial and wavelength degrees of freedom, we experimentally realize high-order tensor-matrix multiplication in a single propagation and process all computational-basis inputs for each 4-qubit gate. Using a physics-based optical propagation model, we further numerically evaluate the architecture for the Deutsch algorithm and for the tensor network of all 128 target instances of a 7-qubit Grover algorithm. These results establish a unified framework for gate-state batch and tensor network simulation, providing a route to exploit optical concurrency across quantum simulation tasks.
authors: Yufeng Zhang, Xuhan Guo, Zixuan Ning, Zhiliang Yuan, Yikai Su, Kaizhi Wang, Sergei Turitsyn, Zhipei Sun

papers.title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
papers.abstract: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$. Together with a theorem of Caldero and Keller, it also decides mutation equivalence of two four-vertex quivers up to relabeling whenever one of them is mutation-acyclic. We conjecture that $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ alone suffices as the bound, which would reduce the search to $O(h^{6})$ states, and we verify this for all four-vertex quivers of height at most three. In the other direction, for every $n\ge4$ we construct an affine family of connected $n$-vertex quivers whose nonnegative even members are mutation-acyclic and whose positive odd members are mutation-cyclic. Consequently, unlike in rank three, no fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial equations and strict polynomial inequalities in the arrow weights (i.e., a semialgebraic criterion) decides mutation-acyclicity of $n$-vertex quivers, even allowing polynomials that are not mutation-invariant. Finally, we correct the criterion for four-vertex quivers of height at most two stated in our earlier paper, and recover its classification counts with short certificates. The calculations in the proof of the height bound are verified by computer for all values of their parameters.
authors: Kymani T. K. Armstrong-Williams, Edward Hirst, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee

papers.title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
papers.abstract: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. This formulation organizes PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture. The resulting framework provides design principles for free-electron modulators that can control energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces, establishing LEM as a device-level platform for programmable femtosecond-to-attosecond matter-wave control.
authors: Zirui Zhao, Ruoyu Chen, Changying Li, Yongcheng Ding, Zhaopin Chen, Xinbing Song, Shuaishuai Sun, Ye Tian, Kangpeng Wang, Yiming Pan

papers.title: One-dimensional second-gradient elasticity: pantograph-inspired energies and solitary waves
papers.abstract: We present a self-contained formulation of longitudinal motion in one-dimensional second-gradient continua. Starting from finite-strain kinematics, we then apply the Principle of Virtual Power to identify the governing field equation and contact actions, derive the balance laws, and establish the mechanical-energy identity for hyperelastic materials. Motivated by pantographic microstructures, we study a class of finite-strain energies formulated in terms of normalized strain measures and deformation-dependent strain-gradient moduli. For the associated equation of motion, a traveling-wave first integral yields a turning-point criterion for the existence of solitary waves with positive stretch, exponential decay, and finite mechanical energy, as well as uniqueness at each fixed speed within a prescribed strain interval. For suitable spring energies, a change of strain variable reduces this integral to a polynomial equation, yielding explicit tensile and compressive profiles for Green--Lagrange and Hencky strains under appropriate parameter and kinematic conditions. Under the positivity condition on the quartic potential, the constructed Hencky energy has several physically natural properties: it is nonnegative, admits the natural state as its unique zero and global minimizer, has a positive linearized modulus, penalizes stretch gradients, and diverges under both material collapse and unlimited extension. Furthermore, the stored energy is coercive with respect to the $H^1$ norm of logarithmic strain. Together with mechanical-energy conservation, this yields uniform upper and positive lower bounds on stretch throughout the lifespan of smooth solutions. The theory's accessible mechanical origin, relatively simple mathematical foundation, and diverse solitary waves offer a tractable entry point to studying the rich nonlinear dispersive equations governing higher-gradient elastic continua.
authors: R. S. Hallyburton, I. Giorgio, C. Rodriguez

papers.title: Non-minimal $\alpha$-attractor magnetogenesis with potential dependent couplings
papers.abstract: We investigate inflationary magnetogenesis driven by a non conformal coupling in the case of large-field $\alpha$-attractor inspired models. We introduce potential-dependent electromagnetic coupling functions $f(\phi)$ that reproduce the scaling $f\propto a^p$ during slow roll. Starting from Starobinsky inflation, we analytically derive explicit couplings for $(E)$-model and $(T)$-model potentials. We then study how these functions affect electromagnetic amplification in the regime of non-minimal coupling between the inflaton field and the Ricci scalar $\phi^2 R$. In particular, we compare different values for the coupling strength $\xi$, accounting for electromagnetic backreaction and Schwinger pair production through the gradient expansion formalism. Our numerical results show that the non-minimal coupling affects the evolution of the electromagnetic sector and the resulting magnetic-field amplitude. We find that, within the analyzed configurations, minimally coupled and $\xi>0$ scenarios are compatible with the adopted CMB constraints, yielding conditional present-day magnetic-field estimates of order $10^{-23}$ G.
authors: Antonino G. Marino, Tommaso Mengoni

papers.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
papers.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with near-optimal quadrature squeezing. The ability to generate a wide variety of Wigner-negative states with mature semiconductor technology opens promising opportunities for continuous-variable optical quantum technologies.
authors: Hubert Lam, Petr Steindl, Yann Portella, Kiarn T. Laverick, Kian Hwee Lim, Juan R. Alvarez, Aristide Lemaitre, Maria Maffei, Alexia Auffeves, Dario A. Fioretto, Pascale Senellart

papers.title: The Keller problem for the lowest positive eigenvalue of Dirac operators with Lorentz scalar potentials
papers.abstract: We study the Keller problem for the Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_m - V\beta$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and minimize its lowest positive eigenvalue over all potentials $V$ with prescribed $L^p$ norm. We prove that optimal potentials always exist and that the corresponding eigenspinors solve the nonlinear Soler equation. This provides a variational proof of existence of solitary waves for this equation. We prove that there are no zero modes for such operators in dimensions $1$ and $2$, and conjecture that zero mode may exist in dimension $3$. In dimension $d = 2$, we provide numerical evidence that the optimal potentials concentrate on flower-shape regions, which are not necessarily radial, showing that Faber--Krahn type results may fail for such Dirac operators. In dimension $1$, all quantities are explicit.
authors: David Gontier, Hanne Van Den Bosch

papers.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
papers.abstract: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-$\beta$ concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.
authors: J. W. Burby, I. Cho, M. Ruth

papers.title: Dynamical Tensor Train Approximation for Wigner--Fokker--Planck Equation with Applications to Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a dynamical tensor-train method for the Wigner--Fokker--Planck equation arising in continuous-variable open quantum systems. The Wigner function is evolved directly in tensor-train form using a projector-splitting integrator, while the nonlocal Wigner pseudo-differential operator is treated through low-rank representations of the potential difference and matrix-free exponential actions. The resulting method avoids full tensor-product computations in high-dimensional phase space. Numerical experiments in one, two, and three spatial dimensions demonstrate the accuracy and scalability of the method, including simulations in a six-dimensional phase space.
authors: Geshuo Wang, Jingwei Hu

papers.title: Towards Quantum Computation of Bulk FeO
papers.abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising path towards efficient calculations of the electronic structure of correlated materials. The properties of iron-based materials, which are key for advancing geological and astrophysical understanding, are notoriously difficult to calculate with classical computers. However, despite the many recent advances in quantum computing on near intermediate scale quantum hardware, a full treatment of the electronic structure of high-$Z$ atoms or molecules remains challenging. Here, we investigate the ground-state properties of molecular FeO and Fe$_2$O$_2$ model Hamiltonians using classical exact diagonalization, Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), and Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD). The experimental quintet ground state of FeO is recovered classically and with quantum algorithms, while a nonet ground state is recovered for Fe$_2$O$_2$. Although raw VQE does not achieve chemical accuracy for the ground state of FeO or Fe$_2$O$_2$, SQD with two connectivity shells recovers the exact ground energy for both molecules utilizing remarkably few quantum computational resources. Overall, our results indicate that $ab \; initio$-informed low-energy models of correlated materials, combined with SQD, offer a new alternative for scaling up calculations of ground-state properties of strongly correlated solids on existing quantum hardware.
authors: Daniel Staros, Federico Petrovich, Ammar Kirmani, Daniel N. Blaschke, M. Cerezo, Jian-Xin Zhu

papers.title: The Disordered Universe 2025: Analytic Properties of Amplitudes and Correlators
papers.abstract: These lectures provide an introduction to modern techniques for studying the analytic properties of loop-level scattering amplitudes and correlation functions in perturbative quantum field theory. We begin by developing the ideas behind Landau analysis, which identifies the location and nature of kinematic singularities in Feynman integrals (the universal building blocks that contribute to perturbative amplitudes and correlators). We then show how fundamental principles such as unitarity and causality constrain the analytic structure of Feynman integrals, and develop methods for working out some of these constraints in practice. Finally, we connect these observations to the properties of iterated integrals and their symbol calculus, to show how bootstrap methods can be used to determine the functional form of Feynman integrals from just knowledge of their analytic structure. These notes are based on a series of lectures held during the La Ricotta Summer School "The Disordered Universe 2025" from 21~July to 1~August~2025.
authors: Mattia Capuano, Chandramouli Chowdhury, Chantelle Esper, Alessandro Palazio, Jonah Stalknecht, Yong Sheng Yap, Andrew J. McLeod, Paolo Benincasa, Guilherme Leite Pimentel

papers.title: Quantum hydrodynamics from Nambu's unpublished fluid notes
papers.abstract: We develop a quantum hydrodynamic theory based on Nambu's unpublished note \emph{A New Look at Fluid Dynamics}. The kinetic action defines a metric on configuration space and a mechanical connection coupling an observable cyclic deformation to unobserved fluid modes. Tracing out these modes yields a quantum channel for the observed deformation. We establish a criterion for the exact preservation of coherence between opposite momenta and show how nonzero connection curvature prevents this coupling from being removed. The leading quadratic decay of quantum coherence is determined by the prepared quantum state. For two shear flows, we identify an exact noiseless sign subsystem. Introducing additional generating flows cancels the initial residual of the Euler equations while producing nonzero connection curvature, governed by the same kinetic integrals that determine the classical correction. At fixed mean energy, choosing amplitudes adapted to the dominant coupling flow substantially reduces the initial decoherence, even along the direction that cancels the Euler residual. This advantage gradually diminishes under conditional evolution, eventually leading to a crossing of the decoherence curves. Our example shows that a preparation with a smaller initial coherence-decay coefficient can have a larger maximum sampled loss over a finite readout interval.
authors: Kazuki Ikeda

papers.title: Quark Saturation in Magnetized Pure Neutron Matter
papers.abstract: We study how magnetic fields affect the onset of quark saturation, which limits the domain of applicability of a purely baryonic description. We consider matter composed of electrically neutral $ddu$ baryons, including neutron- and $\Delta^0$-like states. Using a simple constituent-quark model, we compute the baryon wave functions and spectra in magnetic fields. The magnetic field polarizes the spin-flavor structure, compresses the internal wave function in the transverse direction, and strongly suppresses the transverse kinetic energy. From the baryon wave functions, we construct the one-body reduced density matrix and derive the corresponding single-quark distributions in longitudinal momentum and Landau-level space. We then use these distributions to evaluate quark occupation probabilities in an ideal baryon gas and determine the onset of quark saturation. At finite magnetic field in the $+z$-direction, the $d_\downarrow$ quark in the lowest Landau level reaches saturation first. The resulting saturation density depends nonmonotonically on the magnetic-field strength: it decreases at weak fields and increases at stronger fields. This behavior reflects the competition between spin-flavor polarization, which promotes saturation, and transverse spatial squeezing, which delays saturation by broadening of the quark transverse momentum distribution.
authors: Toru Kojo

papers.title: Ratchet Effects for Swarmalators on Asymmetric Substrates
papers.abstract: Swarmalators are particles which have internal degrees of freedom in the form of phase oscillators that can synchronize and change the dynamics of the particles. We explore the active matter disk swarmalator model proposed by Adorj\'{a}ni [Phys. Rev. E 109, 024607 (2024)] where there is an additional attraction or repulsion determined by whether the phases of particles within a certain radius synchronize or anti-synchronize. This model in the absence of swarmalator rules forms a motility-induced phase-separated (MIPS) state at high activity, but when the swarmalator rules are present, a number of additional states appear including an active gel, labyrinth state, frustrated MIPS, and frustrated fluid states. Here we examine ratchet effects for the Adorj\'{a}ni model coupled to asymmetric substrates. We find that swarmalator interactions can strongly enhance or suppress active matter ratcheting depending on the structural state of the system, and show that the ratchet efficiency depends on the substrate strength, substrate lattice spacing, and the motor force on the particles. The gel state exhibits the weakest ratcheting for small substrate spacing and can even produce a reversed ratchet motion, but shows the strongest ratcheting for large motor forces. The labyrinth state exhibits the strongest ratcheting over a wide range of parameters since the quasi-one-dimensional labyrinth morphology can match the substrate geometry well.
